news_drafts.headline: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority's auditor expects a qualified 2025/26 accounts opinion
news_drafts.lead:
The Combined Authority's external auditor, the accountancy firm EY, expects to issue a qualified opinion on its 2025/26 accounts, meaning it could not fully sign them off. The audit results report put to the Audit and Governance Committee on 12 November says the audit is substantially complete, subject to outstanding procedures. It would be the first audit opinion the Authority has received since 2022/23. The auditor disclaimed its opinion, declining to give one, for both 2023/24 and 2024/25.

The Authority's covering report says the qualification arises from national audit backstop issues, not from errors identified in the accounts. The auditor could not gain assurance over the 2022/23 closing balances, which carry forward into later years. In the report's words, "This opinion is qualified only due to the impact of carried forward balances lacking assurance as a result of the national audit issues identified earlier." The auditor also says it does not currently expect its report to refer to any material uncertainty about the Authority's ability to continue preparing its accounts as an ongoing organisation.

The auditor's draft report anticipates another qualified opinion for 2026/27, as assurance improves, and says an unqualified opinion is possible for 2027/28. The Combined Authority says it wants to discuss with the auditors whether unqualified opinions could return earlier.
news_drafts.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26

news_drafts.headline: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough transport spending is £7.7m so far, against a £10.2m year-to-date budget
news_drafts.lead:
Day-to-day spending on transport at the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough combined authority stands at £7.7m for the year to date, against a year-to-date budget of £10.2m, an underspend of £2.5m. The figures are in the Budget and Performance Report going to the Transport Committee on 4 November.

The report says most of the year-to-date underspend sits in public transport bus services. In its words, "the underspend here is because of a lag in billing from contractors". The report does not present the year-to-date gap as a saving for the year.

The full-year budget for transport is £23.8m and the full-year forecast is £23.7m, a variance of £125k below budget. The report gives a separate reason for that forecast variance: the start of the Market Towns Cycle Support scheme has been delayed and its spending is now spread over three years.

findings.headline: Devolution and Priorities Fund rises from £473k in 2026/27 to £2,547k in 2027/28
findings.detail: The fund stays between £2,027k and £2,547k in each later year shown. The Delegated Funds total moves from £573k in 2026/27 to £2,647k in 2027/28.
findings.matters: A discretionary fund that grows about fivefold in one year is a change in how the Combined Authority plans to use its unallocated resources, which a reader would want to see alongside the reserve position.

findings.headline: Mayoral Capacity Funding balance of £1,311k in 2026/27 is shown as nil from 2027/28
findings.detail: The Mayoral Capacity Fund total moves from £1,311k in 2026/27 to nil in every later year. The paper labels the 2026/27 figure as a balance.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare how a carried-forward funding balance is planned to be fully spent in the year it is available.
findings.figures: Mayoral Capacity Funding balance: £1,311k (2026/27), nil (2027/28 to 2030/31)

findings.headline: Election Costs Total of £1,590k is budgeted in 2028/29, with nil in the other years shown
findings.detail: The Legal and Governance Directorate total is £1,692k in 2026/27 and rises to £3,576k in 2028/29 when the election cost is included. Election costs are shown as nil in the other four years.
findings.matters: A single election cost of this size in one year makes the 2028/29 Legal and Governance total roughly double the other years, which a reader would want to see flagged for reserve or cash planning.
findings.figures: Election Costs Total: £1,590k (2028/29), nil (other years); Legal and Governance Directorate Total: £1,692k (2026/27), £3,576k (2028/29)

findings.headline: Organisational Savings Target of £200k in 2026/27 is shown as nil from 2027/28
findings.detail: The savings line is shown as a negative figure of £200k in 2026/27 with no equivalent in later years. This extract does not show what replaces it.
findings.matters: A savings target that is not carried forward in the plan period is something a finance director would check against the savings tracker, here or at a peer council.
findings.figures: Organisational Savings Target: £200k reduction (2026/27), nil (2027/28 to 2030/31)

findings.headline: Grand total revenue budget is £97,448k in 2026/27, £83,498k in 2027/28 and £119,702k in 2030/31
findings.detail: The total falls in 2027/28 and then rises in each later year, to £101,578k in 2028/29 and £111,218k in 2029/30. The Transport Directorate total moves from £27,669k in 2026/27 to £79,906k in 2030/31.
findings.matters: A total that falls and then grows by over £36,000k across the plan is a sharp change in the revenue profile that finance officers will want to test against funding.

daily_post.headline: Bus franchising capital expenditure of £18.71m is forecast to be debt-financed by 31 March 2027, with no debt-funded spend recorded to 30 September 2026.
daily_post.lead: A finance director would want to know when debt will be needed to fund a major transport scheme, and how it squares with the authorised limit and the zero debt figure in the financing table.
